databaseBackups.databaseBackupsInTheFormatOf: Database backups in the format of supabase db dump: roles, schema and data. Storage files aren't included, as in Supabase's own backups.
databaseBackups.backItsDatabaseUpWhereIt: Back its database up where it runs, for example with supabase db dump. Projects created with “Create a new stack” are backed up from here.
databaseBackups.supermixerConnectsToThisStackIt: Supermixer connects to this stack; it didn't create it
databaseBackups.restoringTheProjectIsOfflineUntil: Restoring; the project is offline until it finishes
databaseBackups.copyingTheBackupToTheBucket: Copying the backup to the bucket
databaseBackups.startTheStackToBackIt: Start the stack to back it up
databaseBackups.theStackIsBusyWaitFor: The stack is busy; wait for it to finish
databaseBackups.setByTheSupermixerServerS: Set by the Supermixer server's configuration (provisioning.backup_interval, backup_keep and backup_s3).
databaseBackups.backedUpEveryWhileRunningThe: Backed up every {{interval}} while running; the newest {{keep}} scheduled backups are kept. Manual backups are kept until you delete them.
databaseBackups.scheduledBackupsAreOffManualBackups: Scheduled backups are off. Manual backups are kept until you delete them.
databaseBackups.backupsAreOnlyOnTheSupermixer: Backups are only on the Supermixer server. Set provisioning.backup_s3 to copy them to an S3-compatible bucket as well.
databaseBackups.theDatabaseIsOfflineUntilThe: The database is offline until the restore finishes. Progress is on Settings › Infrastructure.
databaseBackups.toRestoreADownloadElsewhereAs: To restore a download elsewhere, as Supabase documents: psql --single-transaction -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f roles.sql -f schema.sql -f data.sql. The Vault's secrets aren't included, and roles that log in need their passwords set again.
databaseBackups.restoreThisBackupToTheProject: Restore this backup to the project?
databaseBackups.theDatabaseIsReplacedWithThe: The database is replaced with the backup of {{value}}; changes since then are lost. Supermixer backs the current database up first, and the project is offline while it restores. If the restore fails, the project goes back to its current database.
databaseBackups.supermixerCreatesANewStackIn: Supermixer creates a new stack in this organization, with its own keys, and restores the backup into it. This project isn't changed.
databaseBackups.name: Name
databaseBackups.theBackupIsOnlyInBucket: The backup is only in bucket {{bucket}}, and Supermixer isn’t set up for a bucket.
databaseBackups.theBackupIsOnlyInBucket2: The backup is only in bucket {{bucket}}, and Supermixer is set up for bucket {{current}}.
databaseBackups.itsFilesAreRemovedFromThe: Its files are removed from the Supermixer server.
databaseBackups.itsCopyInBucketIsRemoved: Its copy in bucket {{bucket}} is removed too (later, if Supermixer can’t reach the bucket right now).
databaseBackups.itsCopyInBucketIsRemoved2: Its copy in bucket {{bucket}} is removed once Supermixer is set up for that bucket again.
databaseBackups.supermixerTriesAgainOnItsOwn: Supermixer tries again on its own, waiting longer each time.
databaseBackups.backupsArenTCopiedToA: Backups aren’t copied to a bucket any more, so it won’t be tried again.
databaseBackups.copiedToAndKept: Each backup is copied to {{location}} at {{endpoint}}, and kept on the Supermixer server too.
databaseBackups.copiedToAndRemoved: Each backup is copied to {{location}} at {{endpoint}}; once copied, it’s removed from the Supermixer server.

databaseColumnPrivileges.grantedToPublicSoEveryRole: Granted to PUBLIC, so every role has it
databaseColumnPrivileges.grantedByAnotherRoleSoIt: Granted by another role, so it can't be revoked here
databaseColumnPrivileges.losesOnEveryColumnOfIncluding: {{role}} loses {{p}} on every column of {{schema}}.{{table}}, including any granted column by column.
databaseColumnPrivileges.hasOnTheWholeTableWhich: {{role}} has {{p}} on the whole table, which covers every column. To take {{column}} away, the table grant is replaced by grants on each of the other {{length}} columns. Columns added later won't get {{p2}} until you grant it.
databaseColumnPrivileges.grantedBySoItCanT: Granted by {{join}}, so it can't be revoked here
databaseColumnPrivileges.chooseWhichColumnsOfATable: Choose which columns of a table each role can read and write through the Data API and SQL.
databaseColumnPrivileges.untickingOneColumnOfAPrivilege: Unticking one column of a privilege the role holds table-wide replaces the table grant with grants on each other column, and new columns then aren't covered until you grant them. Privileges a role gets through membership of another role aren't shown. Row Level Security still decides which rows a role sees.
databaseColumnPrivileges.aGrantOnTheWholeTable: A grant on the whole table covers every column
databaseColumnPrivileges.isASuperuserSoPostgresNever: {{name}} is a superuser, so Postgres never checks its privileges.
databaseColumnPrivileges.ownsSoItCanAlwaysGrant: {{owner}} owns {{table}}, so it can always grant itself these privileges back.
databaseColumnPrivileges.noTableOrViewCalledIn: No table or view called {{table}} in {{schema}}
databaseColumnPrivileges.notGrantedOnTheWholeTable: Not granted on the whole table

databaseFunctions.savedWithCreateOrReplaceChanging: Saved with create or replace. Changing the arguments creates a separate function.
databaseFunctions.eGVoidTriggerInt8Setof: e.g. void, trigger, int8, setof public.todos
databaseFunctions.asInSqlEGUser: As in SQL, e.g. user_id uuid, amount numeric default 0
databaseFunctions.securityDefinerRunsWithTheOwner: Security definerRuns with the owner's rights instead of the caller's. Use with care.
databaseFunctions.namesInTheBodyMustBe: Names in the body must be schema-qualified, which prevents search_path attacks.

databaseRoles.rolesThatOwnObjectsOrHold: Roles that own objects or hold privileges can't be dropped until those are reassigned or revoked.
databaseRoles.thatNameIsReservedForSupabase: That name is reserved for Supabase's or Supermixer's own roles.
databaseRoles.neededToConnectGroupRolesUsually: Needed to connect; group roles usually leave it off.
databaseRoles.getsThePrivilegesOfRolesIt: Gets the privileges of roles it is a member of.
databaseRoles.canCreateAlterAndDropOther: Can create, alter and drop other roles.
databaseRoles.canStartStreamingReplicationOnPostgres: Can start streaming replication. On Postgres 15 only a superuser can set this.
databaseRoles.ignoresEveryRlsPolicyUseWith: Ignores every RLS policy. Use with care.
databaseRoles.passwordsAreHashedWithScramSha: Passwords are hashed with SCRAM-SHA-256 in your browser; Postgres only receives the hash. Through the pooler, sign in as {{user}}.
databaseRoles.name: Name
databaseRoles.leaveBlankToKeepTheCurrent: Leave blank to keep the current password. The pooler (Supavisor) caches passwords, so a new one may take a while to work through it; direct connections use it at once.
databaseRoles.leaveBlankForARoleThat: Leave blank for a role that signs in another way, or not at all.
databaseRoles.browsersOnlyAllowPasswordHashingOn: Browsers only allow password hashing on HTTPS or localhost. Open Supermixer over HTTPS, or leave the password blank.
databaseRoles.passwordsCanOnlyBeSetOver: Passwords can only be set over HTTPS
databaseRoles.ifThisRoleSPasswordIs: If this role's password is stored as MD5 (older stacks), Postgres clears it on rename and the role can no longer sign in. Set a new password here to be safe.
databaseRoles.n1OrBlankForNoLimit: -1 or blank for no limit; 0 blocks every connection.
databaseRoles.thePasswordWorksThroughTheEnd: The password works through the end of this day, in your time zone.
databaseRoles.whoCanConnectAndWhatThey_one: Who can connect and what they may do. {{count}} connection open right now.
databaseRoles.whoCanConnectAndWhatThey_other: Who can connect and what they may do. {{count}} connections open right now.
databaseRoles.upTo63Bytes: Up to 63 bytes; names starting with pg_ are reserved.
